chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said:
I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying:

When it was a dark night or there was rain, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform the maghrib prayer, then remain for the amount of time in which the people would perform supererogatory prayers, then his mu'adhdhin would give the iqamah, then he would perform the ʿisha' al-akhirah prayer, and they would depart.

As for the end of the time of the ʿisha' al-akhirah prayer, we have also explained that it extends to one-third of the night, and its furthest limit is until midnight; and that is in cases of necessity and incidental circumstances such as illnesses and important matters. We have already cited reports regarding that, and this further clarifies it.

key_terms.ثُلُثِ اللَّيْلِ: one-third of the night, mentioned as the end of the preferred time
key_terms.لَيْلَةٌ مُظْلِمَةٌ: a very dark night that affects normal conditions of prayer timing
key_terms.مَطَرٌ: rain, mentioned as a circumstance affecting congregational prayer practice
key_terms.مُؤَذِّنُهُ: his mu'adhdhin, the one who calls or signals the prayer
key_terms.نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ: midnight, mentioned as the furthest limit in necessity

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the time of maghrib and ʿisha' prayers on dark or rainy nights?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the timing of maghrib and ʿisha' al-akhirah, especially under difficult conditions such as darkness or rain. It shows the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in delaying ʿisha' slightly after maghrib and indicates that the extended latest time for ʿisha' reaches midnight in cases of necessity.
